_note: Real / plausible notable weather across NV/CA/AZ/UT, Nov 7 - Dec 31 2025. Overlaid on the deterministic climatology in weather.py: when 'today' falls in a window and the place matches region/zone, the day's weather is pushed toward these values (colder lows, more precip/wind, snow where it's high and cold). These anchor the 'outrace the storm / get stuck' beats and the cold mornings. zone = poi_ids most affected; regions = whole-state fallback. hook: first_closure | warm_window | cold_snap | outrace | wind.

events.what: the first real snow drops on the high Sierra — Tioga's gate comes down for the winter and the eastern passes start to whiten
the season's first storm stacks up against the Wasatch — Cottonwood canyons go white overnight
a fat ridge of high pressure parks over the Southwest — bluebird days, the resorts grumbling about bare runs, the desert flat-out gorgeous
a cold front rakes the Mogollon Rim — Flagstaff and the canyon rims pick up the first plowable snow
an arctic airmass pours down out of the Great Basin — single-digit mornings, ice fog in the valleys, batteries dying all over the Wasatch Front
the barometer's falling and the air's gone still — every radio in the eastern Sierra is talking about the big system three days out
the big one — a week-long Sierra winter storm dumps feet of snow on the crest. Every pass is chained, R3, or shut; I-80 over Donner closes in waves
a Christmas atmospheric river slams the coast — sheeting rain, flooded lowland on-ramps, surf advisories from Monterey to Malibu
the same trough buries the Wasatch — Little Cottonwood goes interlodge, the I-15 corridor white-knuckle and slow
a dry windstorm rips down the Vegas valley — 40-mph gusts, blowing grit, high-profile rigs flipped on I-15
winter storm warnings across the high country — Flagstaff and the canyon rims get a hard, plowable foot
the storm track finally lifts — clear, dead-cold New Year's mornings, every windshield frosted to the trim
